\begin{frame}{Combinatorics review/ 3 types of Questions}

\vspace{-.75cm}
\begin{columns}


\column{3.75cm}

\ex{1}{}{How many ways can you roll two 6 sided dice?}\vspace{-.25cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item <4->can repeat
\item <4->[](replacement)
\item []
\item []
\end{itemize}
\begin{block}<5->{Fundamental Priniple of Counting}
\end{block}
\begin{itemize}
\item <6->[]$6$\only<7->{$\times6$} \only<8->{$=36$}
\end{itemize}

\column{3.75cm}

\ex{2}{}{How many ways can 3 people have different birthdays?}\vspace{-.25cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item <9->\textbf{cannot} repeat
\item <10->[](\textbf{no }replacement)
\item <11->Order \textbf{does }matter.
\end{itemize}
\begin{block}<12->{Permutation} \begin{center}$_{n}P_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}$\end{center}
\end{block}
\only<13->{$_{365}P_{3}$\only<14->{ $=\frac{365!}{(365-3)!}$}

\only<15->{ \hspace{0cm}\hphantom{X}$=\frac{365!}{362!}=\frac{365\cdot364\cdot362}{1}$}}

\column{3.75cm}

\ex{3}{}{How many ways can you select 5 numbers 1-40?}\vspace{-.25cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item <16->\textbf{cannot} repeat
\item <16->[](\textbf{no }replacement)
\item <17->Order \textbf{does not }matter.
\end{itemize}
\begin{block}<18->{Combination} \begin{center}$_{n}C_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!r!}$\end{center}
\end{block}
\only<19->{$_{40}C_{5}$\only<20->{ $=\frac{40!}{(40-5)!5!}$}

\only<21->{\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{X}$=\frac{40!}{35!5!}=\frac{40\cdot39\cdot38\cdot37\cdot36}{120}$}}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Combinatorics \& Probability: 3 types of Questions}

\vspace{-.75cm}
\addtocounter{countEx}{-3} %sets ex counter for previous slide
\begin{columns}


\column{3.75cm}

\ex{1}{}{How many ways can you roll two 6 sided dice?}

\column{3.75cm}
\begin{alertblock}<2->{Problem}
 What is the probability that someone rolls a 3 then a 2? 
\end{alertblock}

\column{3.75cm}

\end{columns}

\begin{columns}


\column{11cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item []
\item <3->[]$p(3\mbox{ and }2)$\only<4->{ $=\dfrac{n(3\mbox{ and }2)}{n(S)}$}\only<5->{ $=\dfrac{1}{36}$}
\end{itemize}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Combinatorics \& Probability: 3 types of Questions}

\vspace{-.75cm}
\begin{columns}


\column{3.75cm}

\column{3.75cm}

\ex{1}{}{How many ways can 3 people have different birthdays?}\vspace{-.25cm}

\column{3.75cm}
\begin{alertblock}<2->{Problem}
 What is the probability at least 2 out of 3 people have the same
birthday?
\end{alertblock}
\end{columns}

\begin{itemize}
\item <3->\textbf{Same as asking: }\emph{``What is the probability that
3 people }\textbf{\emph{do not }}\emph{have different birthdays?''}\vspace{-.5cm}
\end{itemize}
\begin{columns}


\column{6.5cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item <4->[$S:$] All possible birthdays for 3 people.
\item <5->[$E:$] Of 3 people, some have the same birthday.
\item <6->[$E':$] 3 people have different birthdays.
\end{itemize}

\column{5.5cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item []<7->$p(E')$\uncover<8->{ $=\dfrac{n(E')}{n(S)}$}\uncover<9->{ $=\dfrac{_{365}P_{5}}{365^{3}}$}
\item []<10->$p(E)$\uncover<11->{ $=1-p(E')$}\\
\vspace{5pt} \uncover<12->{\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)$ }$=1-\dfrac{_{365}P_{5}}{365^{3}}$}\\
\vspace{5pt} \uncover<13->{\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)$ }$=0.008204\dots$}\\
\uncover<14->{\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)$ }$\approx0.8\%$}
\end{itemize}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Combinatorics \& Probability: 3 types of Questions}

\vspace{-.75cm}
\begin{columns}


\column{3.75cm}

\column{3.75cm}
\begin{alertblock}<2->{Problem}
 What is the probability that someone matches 5 randomly drawn numbers
from 1-40?
\end{alertblock}

\column{3.75cm}

\ex{1}{}{How many ways can you select 5 numbers 1-40?}\vspace{-.25cm}
\end{columns}

\begin{itemize}
\item <3->A \textbf{5/40} lottery game.\vspace{-.5cm}
\end{itemize}
\begin{columns}


\column{6.5cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item <4->[$S:$] All possible number selections. 
\item <5->[$E:$] Selection matches the drawn number.

\begin{itemize}
\item <6->Order does not matter.
\item <7->[ex.]If $\{10,11,20,40,1\}$ is the drawn then the selection
$\{1,11,40,1,20\}$ wins \nth{1} prize. 
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

\column{5.5cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item []<8->$p(E)$\uncover<9->{ $=\dfrac{n(E)}{n(S)}$}\uncover<10->{ $=\dfrac{1}{_{40}C_{5}}$}\\
\vspace{5pt} \uncover<11->{\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)$ }$=\dfrac{1}{\left(\nicefrac{40\cdot39\cdot38\cdot37\cdot36}{120}\right)}$}\\
\vspace{5pt} \uncover<12->{\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)$ }$=\dfrac{1}{7,059,052}$}\\
\vspace{5pt} \uncover<13->{\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)$ }$\approx0.00001417\%$}
\end{itemize}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Problems}

\prob{1}{}{A group of 30 people is selected at random}{What is the
probability that at least two of them have the same birthday?}
\begin{itemize}
\item <2->[]$n(S)=365^{30}\approx7.39241\cdot10^{76}$ (very big) 
\item <3->[]Let $E:$ At least two have the same birthday.
\item <4->[]$n(E')=$\uncover<5->{$_{365}P_{30}\approx2.171103\cdot10^{76}$
(also very big)}
\item []
\item <6->[]$p(E)=$\uncover<7->{$1-p(E')=1-\dfrac{n(E')}{n(S)}$}
\item []<7->\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)=$$1-p(E')$}$=1-\dfrac{_{365}P_{30}}{365^{30}}$
\item []<8->\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)=$$1-p(E')$}$\approx.7063$
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Problems}

\prob{1}{}{A group of 35 people is selected at random}{What is the
probability that at least two of them have the same birthday?}
\begin{itemize}
\item <2->[]$n(S)=365^{35}$ 
\item <3->[]Let $E:$ At least two have the same birthday.
\item <4->[]$n(E')=$\uncover<5->{$_{365}P_{35}$}
\item []
\item <6->[]$p(E)=$\uncover<7->{$1-p(E')=1-\dfrac{n(E')}{n(S)}$}
\item []<7->\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)=$$1-p(E')$}$=1-\dfrac{_{365}P_{35}}{365^{35}}$
\item []<8->\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(E)=$$1-p(E')$}$\approx.8144$
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Problems}

\prob{1}{1}{}{What is the least number you would need in a group
so that there is a probability of \emph{at least }$78\%$?}
\begin{itemize}
\item <2->[]From the last two problems we know the answer is between $30$
and $35$
\item <3->[]$p(E_{30})=$$1-p(E_{30}')=1-\dfrac{_{365}P_{30}}{365^{30}}\approx.7063$
\item <5->[]$p(E_{31})=$$1-p(E_{31}')=1-\dfrac{_{365}P_{31}}{365^{31}}\approx.7305$
\item <6->[]$p(E_{32})=$$1-p(E_{32}')=1-\dfrac{_{365}P_{32}}{365^{32}}\approx.7533$
\item <7->[]$p(E_{33})=$$1-p(E_{33}')=1-\dfrac{_{365}P_{33}}{365^{33}}\approx.7749$
\item []<8->$p(E_{34})=$$1-p(E_{34}')=1-\dfrac{_{365}P_{34}}{365^{34}}\approx.7953$\uncover<9->{ $\leftarrow$above
$78\%$}
\item []<4->$p(E_{35})=$$1-p(E_{35}')=1-\dfrac{_{365}P_{35}}{365^{35}}$$\approx.8144$
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Problems}

\prob{1}{1}{A state lottery has a 5/40 game (pick 5 different numbers
from 1-40).}{
\begin{enumerate}
\item [a.]Find the probability of winning \nth{1} prize (selecting all
the numbers correctly).
\end{enumerate}
\begin{itemize}
\item [b.]Find the probability of winning \nth{2} prize (selecting all
but one of the numbers correctly).
\end{itemize}
}
\begin{itemize}
\item []
\item [a.]<2->$p(1^{\mbox{st}})=\dfrac{n(1^{\mbox{st}})}{n(S)}$\\
\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(1^{\mbox{st}})$}\textrm{$=\dfrac{_{5}C_{5}}{_{40}C_{5}}\begin{array}{l}
\leftarrow\mbox{ways to choose 5 of 5 winning numbers}\\
\leftarrow\mbox{ways to choose 40 of 5 numbers}
\end{array}$}\\
\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(1^{\mbox{st}})$}$=\dfrac{1}{658008}\approx0.000002$
\item []
\item [b.]<3->$n(2^{\mbox{nd}})=(\mbox{ways to pick }4\mbox{ winners})\times(\mbox{ways to choose \ensuremath{1}loser})$\\
\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$n(E)$}$=_{5}C_{4}\times_{35}C_{1}=5\times35=175$\\
$p(2^{\mbox{nd}})=\dfrac{n(2^{\mbox{nd}})}{n(S)}=\dfrac{175}{658008}\approx.000266$ 
\item <4->Note: $_{35}C_{1}=35=(40-5)$, the non-winning numbers.
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Problems}

\prob{1}{}{5 cards are dealt (without replacement) from a standard
52 card deck.}{Find the probability of being dealt $2$ aces, $2$
queens, and a king?}
\begin{itemize}
\item []<2->Total number of hands, $n(S)=$\uncover<3->{ $_{52}C_{5}$
(order doesn't matter)}
\item []<4->Number of ways to get $2$ aces, $n(2\mbox{A})=$\uncover<5->{ $_{4}C_{2}$
}
\item []<6->Number of ways to get $2$ queens, $n(2\mbox{Q})=$\uncover<7->{ $_{4}C_{2}$
}
\item []<8->Number of ways to get a king, $n(1\mbox{K})=$\uncover<9->{ $_{4}C_{1}$
}
\item []
\item []<10->$p(2\mbox{A}\cap2\mbox{Q}\cap1\mbox{K})=\dfrac{n(2\mbox{A}\cap2\mbox{Q}\cap1\mbox{K})}{n(S)}=$\uncover<11->{ $\dfrac{n(2\mbox{A})\times n(2\mbox{Q})\times n(1\mbox{K})}{n(S)}$}
\item []<12->\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$p(2\mbox{A}\cap2\mbox{Q}\cap1\mbox{K})$}$=\dfrac{_{4}C_{2}\times_{4}C_{2}\times_{4}C_{1}}{_{52}C_{5}}=\dfrac{6\times6\times4}{2598960}=\dfrac{3}{54145}$
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Problems}

\prob{1}{}{You order 12 burritos to go, 5 with peppers and 7 without
peppers. However the restaurant did not label the burritos. If you
pick 3 burritos at random find the probability of each of the follow:}{None
have peppers.}
\begin{itemize}
\item []<2->\textbf{Need to find:}\\
 $p(NP)=\dfrac{n(NP)}{n(S)}=\dfrac{\mbox{ways to pick 3 w/no peppers}}{\mbox{ways to pick }3\mbox{ burritos}}$
\item []<3->$n(S)=$\uncover<4->{ $_{12}C_{3}=220$}
\item []<5->$n(NP)=$\uncover<6->{ $_{7}C_{3}=35$}
\item []
\item []<7->$p(NP)=\dfrac{_{7}C_{3}}{_{12}C_{3}}=\dfrac{35}{220}=\dfrac{7}{44}$
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Problems}

\prob{1}{1}{You order 12 burritos to go, 5 with peppers and 7 without
peppers. If you pick 3 burritos at random find the probability of
each of the follow:}{Exactly 2 have no peppers.}
\begin{itemize}
\item []<2->\textbf{Need to find:}\\
 $p(NP)=\dfrac{n(2P)}{n(S)}=\dfrac{\mbox{ways to pick 2 w/no peppers}}{\mbox{ways to pick }3\mbox{ burritos}}$
\item []<3->$n(S)=$\uncover<4->{ $_{12}C_{3}=220$}
\item []<5->$n(2P)=$\scriptsize $(\mbox{ways to pick 2 w/no peppers})\times(\mbox{ways to pick 1 w/peppers})$\\
\normalsize \hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$n(2P)$}\uncover<6->{ $=_{7}C_{2}\times_{5}C_{1}=21\times5=105$}
\item []
\item []<7->$p(2P)=\dfrac{_{7}C_{2}\times_{5}C_{1}}{_{12}C_{3}}=\dfrac{105}{220}=\dfrac{21}{44}$
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Problems}

\prob{1}{1}{You order 12 burritos to go, 5 with peppers and 7 without
peppers. However the restaurant did not label the burritos. If you
pick 3 burritos at random find the probability of each of the follow:}{At
least 1 has no peppers.}
\begin{itemize}
\item []<2->Equivalently, 1 OR 2 OR 3 have peppers.

\begin{itemize}
\item At least, at most, more than, greater than, etc. $\rightarrow$ \textbf{or
$\rightarrow$ add}
\end{itemize}
\item []<3->\textbf{Need to find:}\\
 $p(NP)=\dfrac{n(NP\geq1)}{n(S)}=\dfrac{\mbox{ways to get at least 1 w/no peppers}}{\mbox{ways to pick }3\mbox{ burritos}}$ 
\item []<4->$n(S)=$\uncover<5->{ $_{12}C_{3}=220$}
\item []<6->$n(NP\geq1)=$\uncover<10->{$70+105+35$}\scriptsize \\
\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$n(P\geq 1)$}\\
\begin{tabular}{ccccc}
\textrm{$n(\mbox{1 w/no peppers})$} &  &  &  & \tabularnewline
\textrm{$+n(\mbox{2 w/no peppers})$} &  &  &  & \tabularnewline
\textrm{$+n(\mbox{3 w/no peppers})$} &  &  &  & \tabularnewline
\end{tabular}\\
\begin{tabular}{crcrl}
 & \only<8->{$n(\mbox{1 w/no peppers})\times n(\mbox{pick 2 w/peppers})$} &  & \only<8->{$_{7}C_{1}\times_{5}C_{2}$} & \only<8->{$70$}\tabularnewline
\only<7->{$=$} & \only<7->{$+n(\mbox{2 w/no peppers})\times n(\mbox{pick 1 w/peppers})$} & \only<7->{$=$} & \only<7->{$+_{7}C_{2}\times_{5}C_{1}$} & \only<7->{$105$}\tabularnewline
 & \only<9->{$+n(\mbox{3 w/no peppers})\times n(\mbox{pick 0 w/peppers})$} &  & \only<9->{$+_{7}C_{3}\times_{5}C_{0}$} & \only<9->{$35$}\tabularnewline
\end{tabular}\normalsize
\item []
\item []<11->$p(NP\geq1)=\dfrac{70+105+35}{220}=\dfrac{210}{220}=\dfrac{21}{22}$\uncover<12->{ ($1-p(\mbox{all peppers})=1-\dfrac{_{5}c_{3}}{220}$)}
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}
